original_question: In the generator coordinate method for quadrupole collective phenomena, how reliable are the collective masses or inertia functions computed using real generator coordinates, and how should one choose or determine the generator coordinates so that the resulting collective description captures both the coordinates and the momenta needed for correct large-amplitude dynamics?
target_in_paper: “A long-standing open problem in the GCM is the reliability of the collective masses (inertial functions) evaluated with the real generator coordinates. For the center of mass motion, complex generator coordinates are needed to reproduce the correct mass, indicating that we have to explicitly treat the collective momenta in addition to the coordinates [7]. Another important problem in the GCM is the choice of the generator coordinates.”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the two central issues raised in section 4.2 of the paper: (1) the reliability of collective masses or inertial functions computed with real generator coordinates, and (2) the need to determine an appropriate set of generator coordinates that incorporate both coordinates and momenta for large-amplitude dynamics.
missing_details: Definition of the generator coordinate method (GCM) in the context of quadrupole collective phenomena and its parametrization by mean-field states
Explanation that ‘collective mass’ refers to the inertial function appearing in the Bohr-Mottelson collective Hamiltonian derived via GCM-GOA
Clarification of what is meant by ‘real’ vs ‘complex’ generator coordinates and why complex coordinates capture momentum degrees of freedom [7]
Specification that the reliability issue arises when applying the Gaussian overlap approximation (GOA) to the GCM equation with real coordinates
Identification of Holzwarth and Yukawa’s variational determination of the generator coordinate [27] as the only existing approach toward optimal coordinate selection
Quantifiers on the scope: the question pertains to one-dimensional quadrupole collective paths in doubly even nuclei
Notation for generator coordinate q, collective momentum p, and their conjugate relationship
Context that the question remains open and is explicitly listed under open problems in section 4.2
refined_question: In the generator coordinate method applied to one-dimensional quadrupole collective motion in even–even nuclei, the Gaussian overlap approximation is used to derive a collective Hamiltonian H(q,p) with an inertial function M(q) evaluated using real generator coordinates q. (i) How accurate and reliable are the resulting inertial functions M(q) when time-odd mean-field effects and collective momenta p are neglected? (ii) Given that reproducing the correct collective mass for center-of-mass motion requires introducing complex generator coordinates to treat p explicitly [7], what microscopic prescription or variational principle can be used to select or determine the real generator coordinates q in the quadrupole GCM so that both the coordinate dependence q and its conjugate momentum p are consistently accounted for, ensuring a faithful description of large-amplitude dynamics?
justification: The refined question is directly taken from section 4.2 of J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys. 37 (2010) 064018 [turn10view0], clarifying definitions (GCM, inertial function, GOA), scope (quadrupole motion in doubly even nuclei), notation (q,p,M(q)), and explicitly mentioning the need to treat time-odd effects and momenta. It remains faithful to the paper’s original two-part open problem without broadening the scope, and it is self-contained.
